content:
incident-bot: PAGER — hosted-runtime-us-east-1: sustained memory growth in KV cache process on replicas [r3,r4,r7]. Multiple OOMs in the last 12m, 5xx spike ~8%. trace=abc12345. paging policy: SEV2

sara (oncall): ack. taking lead. linking runbook now -> https://redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-oom

mike: pulled logs from r3, seeing repeated growth after long prompts (>65k tokens). snippet: `kv_cache.cc: alloc failed at 0x7f9d... size=4294967296` and continuous-batching queue depth climbs to 120.

jess: that matches the hypothesis: runaway context window + continuous batching = unbounded KV retention. we should cut batching and force per-request evictions for hosted tier.

alex: agree. propose hotfix: set continuous_batching.enabled=false for hosted-runtime, and set batch.max_tokens=1024. canary to 5% first.

mike: also recommend TTL on prefix cache entries: `ttl_seconds=600` to avoid long-lived entries from extreme prompts.

sara (oncall): priority: mitigate customer impact first. list of affected customers?

lisa (support): CS report queue shows 3 customers with increased error rates, 2 on enterprise plans (acct ids red-447, red-902). notifying AMs.

jess: rolling mitigation steps: 1) canary disable batching 5% 2) monitor mem/gc 3) if stable, roll to 100% 4) optionally route heavy seq requests to smaller model variant.

infra-bot: ACTION: creating config patch for hosted-runtime-us-east-1
Patch preview:
```
{
  "continuous_batching": { "enabled": false },
  "batch": { "max_tokens": 1024 },
  "kv_cache": { "ttl_seconds": 600 }
}
```

infra-bot: starting canary rollout (5% traffic) -> hosted-runtime-config v2026.03.11-hotfix-ctx

deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded on 3/3 canary hosts. metric check in progress.

mike: canary metrics: mem usage on canary hosts dropped 70% within 2 minutes of deploy. no OOMs during canary window. batching queue depth back to <8.

alex: rolling to 100% now. CLI: `infractl rollout apply --target hosted-runtime-us-east-1 --config v2026.03.11-hotfix-ctx --strategy rolling`

infra-bot: rollout in progress: 30% -> 60% -> 100%

deploy-bot: full rollout complete. all hosts report new config.

sara (oncall): monitoring dashboards show error rate back to baseline. CPU slightly up but within SLO. marking incident mitigated for now.

lisa (support): sending update to impacted customers: "We've applied an infrastructure patch to mitigate memory growth causing 5xx errors. Services are stable. We're following up with a detailed post-incident summary."

jess: action items for postmortem: - root cause analysis on why TTL/default limits didn't kick in - add guard rails: per-request max-kv-entries and global allocation caps - add synthetic tests for very long prompt patterns - consider auto-fallback: when continuous batching sees >N tokens/req, switch to safe path

mike: also adding a temporary monitoring alert: high kv-cache growth per-request (rate > 0.5% of requests) -> auto-disable batching and notify oncall.

alex: created PR for safe-path logic and the TTL change: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8421 —adding code owner reviews.

sara (oncall): will open an incident Slack postmortem thread and assign owners. I’ll file a Sev2 postmortem and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

incident-bot: NOTE: Customer impact window: 2026-03-11T21:30:00Z -> 2026-03-11T21:50:00Z. Estimated affected requests: ~12k, error uplift peak +8%.

alex: tagging followups: @eng-runtime, @eng-ml — need kernel-level analysis of kv memory accounting.

jess: small follow-up hotfix we should still land: clamp `batch.max_tokens` on the public API to 200k tokens for hosted to prevent user-side runaway prompts.

lisa (support): filed CS tickets and created a customer-facing status note in the portal.

sara (oncall): wrap up: incident mitigated and rolled back to stable config with protective limits. next steps: 24h observation, postmortem doc, deploy safer default configs. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
